title: Delivery pipeline loop gates
description: Fail-closed gates wiring the ticket-delivery conveyor into the GSD loop: a blocking plan:post gate runs the ticket-graph validator (Gate 2), so a decomposition without materialized, valid PLAN files cannot pass planning.

delivery_pipeline.graph_gate.description: Run the delivery-pipeline ticket-graph validator as a blocking plan:post gate (mechanical Gate 2).

delivery_pipeline.uat_gate.description: Block ship until the phase has verification evidence (fail-closed `phase uat-passed` predicate at ship:pre).

delivery_pipeline.arch_verdict.description: Advisory ship:pre agent verdict: check the phase's changes against locked ADR decisions in .planning/architecture/ and surface violations before shipping.

delivery_pipeline.sentinel.description: PR sentinel: 'auto' leaves a guard on the open PRs (a background agent where the runtime has one, otherwise a mandatory duty pass each round) so delivery can cascade onward; 'off' keeps every PR in the main loop.

delivery_pipeline.auto_merge.description: Ticket-PR landing: 'epic' lets the sentinel squash a green + arch-conform ticket PR into its base (phase epic or parent ticket branch) once the gate is re-verified against live GitHub; 'off' leaves every merge to a human. The epic -> integration-branch PR is NEVER auto-merged, and human_checkpoint tickets are always excluded.

delivery_pipeline.codex_models.description: The Codex model palette, in preference order: 'model[:effort][@min_cli]' per entry, comma separated. The effort is the one to USE for that model, never the deepest it accepts; min_cli is the Codex CLI version that can first configure it, below which the generator writes the previous entry instead. First entry is the workhorse floor every agent gets; last is the ceiling, taken statically by the integrator and reachable elsewhere through the '-deep' escalation agents. An empty value writes no model at all, leaving every agent on the CLI default. 'gpt-5.6-sol' is a valid entry no built-in path selects: with the deeper efforts retired on this runtime, advertising 'ultra' was its only distinguishing property.

delivery_pipeline.fable.description: Consent for the paid 1M-context ceiling (Claude Fable 5.1). 'off' - the conveyor never emits the 'fable' alias: the three escalation routes (a measured input over fable_window_tokens, a repair whose failure signature came back a third time, a contested judgement) degrade to 'opus' at 'max' effort and print the reason. 'auto' - a person has answered Fable's consent prompt interactively, so those routes are honoured. It defaults to off because an unconsented request in a background session waits out dialogExpiry and then ends the turn without sending, and silence is not consent. No role takes it by default, the integrator included.

delivery_pipeline.fable_window_tokens.description: The window route's threshold: a dispatch whose caller-measured input exceeds this many tokens earns the 1M-context ceiling (when delivery_pipeline.fable is 'auto'). The default is five times the largest input measured on this repository - the phase epic diff, which is the integrator's own input, at 210 KB or about 52k tokens. The caller measures and passes --input-tokens; the resolver only compares, and an absent measurement can never fire the route.

delivery_pipeline.merge_without_ci.description: Set this only in a repository that genuinely has no CI. A pull request with NO reported checks is not a green pull request - nothing ran - so by default both the board and the sentinel withhold the two actions that walk it towards landing (the squash merge, and readying it out of draft) and report the merge as a human's. With this true, an empty check list counts as green again and the sentinel lands such a pull request itself.

delivery_pipeline.max_concurrent_agents.description: How many agents a delivery wave may hold at once. The one axis no choice of model tier can address: the model policy is per dispatch while a spend limit is per session, so what decides whether a run survives is how many dispatches are open together. The default 4 is a measurement - the largest wave this project has completed without an interruption - not a round number. The unit is the AGENT, not the dispatch record: every role counts against it, the PR sentinel included, but one sentinel holding four guarded pull requests is one agent, because the loop marks a record per guarded ticket and spawns a single guard for the round. Counting records instead reported a full board on the ordinary mid-phase one and launched no executor until a pull request merged. The board reports it as capacity {max, in_flight, free} and the delivery loop builds each wave from capacity.free, so a wave wider than the cap is cut rather than refused and the remainder is taken on the next round. The three mechanisms that read it agree: the board declines to call a capped board finished, the CI waiter stops naming work beyond the cap as work to take first, and the stop hook treats a full board as an agent being out rather than as a stop to refuse. A malformed value falls back to the default with a warning; a project config that does not parse authorizes no dispatch at all, because then no policy is in effect and a dispatch is a mutation.

agentVerdict.prompt: Architecture conformance (advisory). If .planning/architecture/ contains no ADR-*.md, verdict: pass. Otherwise: extract locked decisions and scope fences from every ADR (plus INTERFACES.md/DATA-MODEL.md when present), diff the phase's implemented changes (merge-base..HEAD), and judge conformance only against recorded decisions — style and bugs belong to other reviewers. Report each violation as file:line + the violated ADR section + minimal remediation direction. If the code is right and a decision no longer fits reality, say adr-outdated and name the decision — changing it is the human's call. Never block; this verdict is advisory context for the ship decision.
